words.meaning: Excessive pride or confidence that makes a person ignore danger or good advice.
words.example: The captain's hubris led him to sail into the storm, ignoring every warning.

words.meaning: A person who attacks or criticizes popular beliefs or traditional institutions.
words.example: The young artist was seen as an iconoclast for rejecting every rule taught in art school.

words.meaning: A unique habit, mannerism, or way of behaving that is particular to one person.
words.example: Tapping his pencil three times before every test was just one of his odd idiosyncrasies.

words.meaning: Not telling the truth; dishonest and likely to lie.
words.example: The mendacious witness changed his story three times during the trial.

words.meaning: To fix an idea or attitude firmly in someone's mind through repeated teaching.
words.example: Good coaches try to inculcate discipline in young athletes from their very first practice.

words.meaning: Never getting tired; able to keep working or trying without stopping.
words.example: The indefatigable volunteers worked all night to prepare meals for the flood victims.

words.meaning: Extremely poor; lacking the basic things needed to live.
words.example: The charity collects blankets and food every winter for indigent families in the city.

words.meaning: Impossible to stop or change; continuing steadily no matter what.
words.example: The inexorable rise of the floodwaters forced the villagers to leave their homes.

words.meaning: Harmful or unfriendly, especially in a way that works against something's success.
words.example: Constant noise from the construction site was inimical to the students' concentration during exams.

words.meaning: Rude and disrespectful, especially by not showing proper respect to someone in authority.
words.example: The teacher scolded the boy for making an impertinent remark about her handwriting.

words.meaning: Showing a relaxed lack of concern or worry; carefree.
words.example: Despite the looming exam, she walked into class with an insouciant smile, as if nothing worried her.

words.meaning: Seeming to last forever; endless, especially in a boring or tiring way.
words.example: The interminable school assembly made everyone glance at the clock every few minutes.

words.meaning: Difficult to control, manage, or solve.
words.example: The committee faced an intractable problem when neither side was willing to compromise.

words.meaning: Having a habit so long-established that it is unlikely to change.
words.example: Her grandfather was an inveterate storyteller who could turn any small event into an adventure.

words.meaning: Traveling from place to place, especially for work, rather than staying in one location.
words.example: The itinerant musician played in a different town almost every week of the year.

words.meaning: To throw away or get rid of something that is no longer wanted or needed.
words.example: The sinking ship's crew had to jettison heavy cargo to keep it afloat.

words.meaning: Fond of joking; cheerful and playful in manner.
words.example: The jocular uncle kept the whole family laughing with his silly stories at dinner.

words.meaning: A huge, powerful force or thing that cannot be stopped.
words.example: The visiting team was a juggernaut, winning every match of the tournament with ease.

words.meaning: A person who moves, acts, or progresses more slowly than others.
words.example: The teacher gently encouraged the laggard at the back of the group to keep up with the hike.

words.meaning: Slow-moving and relaxed, often from tiredness or a lack of energy or urgency.
words.example: On the hot afternoon, the cat stretched out in a languid pose under the shady tree.
